plain_en: positive traits grouped into virtue categories
definition: a classification system to identify positive traits; organized into categories of wisdom, courage, humanity, justice, temperance, and transcendence.

plain_en: Weakest stimulus detectable half the time
definition: the minimum stimulus energy needed to detect a particular stimulus 50 percent of the time.

plain_en: Eye lens changing shape to focus
definition: in sensation and perception, the process by which the eye's lens changes shape to focus images of near or far objects on the retina.

plain_en: Adjusting schemas to fit new information
definition: in developmental psychology, adapting our current schemas (understandings) to incorporate new information.

plain_en: Drive to accomplish and master high standards
definition: a desire for significant accomplishment, for mastery of skills or ideas, for control, and for attaining a high standard.

plain_en: Test measuring what someone has learned
definition: a test designed to assess what a person has learned.

plain_en: Initial learning stage linking stimuli or strengthening responses
definition: in classical conditioning, the initial stage, when one links a neutral stimulus and an unconditioned stimulus so that the neutral stimulus begins triggering the conditioned response. In operant conditioning, the strengthening of a reinforced response.

plain_en: Brief electrical charge traveling down an axon
definition: a neural impulse; a brief electrical charge that travels down an axon.

plain_en: Empathic listening that echoes and clarifies
definition: empathic listening in which the listener echoes, restates, and seeks clarification. A feature of Rogers' person-centered therapy.

plain_en: Actors blame situations, observers blame persons
definition: the tendency for those acting in a situation to attribute their behavior to external causes, but for observers to attribute others' behavior to internal causes. This contributes to the fundamental attribution error (which focuses on our explanations for others' behavior).

plain_en: Schizophrenia with sudden onset and likely recovery
definition: (also called reactive schizophrenia) a form of schizophrenia that can begin at any age; frequently occurs in response to a traumatic event, and from which recovery is much more likely.

plain_en: Judging relative to our prior experience level
definition: our tendency to form judgments (of sounds, of lights, of income) relative to a neutral level defined by our prior experience.

plain_en: everyday word for harmful compulsive use
definition: an everyday term for compulsive substance use (and sometimes for dysfunctional behavior patterns, such as out-of-control gambling) that continue despite harmful consequences. (See also substance use disorder.)

plain_en: growing from child to adult
definition: the transition period from childhood to adulthood, extending from puberty to independence.

plain_en: heart-lung exercise that also calms anxiety
definition: sustained exercise that increases heart and lung fitness; also helps alleviate anxiety.

plain_en: need for relationships and group belonging
definition: the need to build and maintain relationships and to feel part of a group.

plain_en: behavior meant to hurt someone
definition: any physical or verbal behavior intended to harm someone physically or emotionally.

plain_en: molecule that boosts a neurotransmitter
definition: a molecule that increases a neurotransmitter's action.

plain_en: fear of places where panic may strike
definition: fear or avoidance of situations, such as crowds or wide open places, where one may experience a loss of control and panic.

plain_en: step-by-step method that always solves a problem
definition: a methodical, logical rule or procedure that guarantees solving a particular problem. Contrasts with the usually speedier -but also more error-prone -use of heuristics.

plain_en: neuron fires fully or not at all
definition: a neuron's reaction of either firing (with a full-strength response) or not firing.

plain_en: slow brain waves of relaxed wakefulness
definition: the relatively slow brain waves of a relaxed, awake state.

plain_en: selfless concern for others' well-being
definition: unselfish regard for the welfare of others.

plain_en: brain clusters linked to emotion
definition: [uh-MIG-duh-la] two lima-bean-sized neural clusters in the limbic system; linked to emotion.

plain_en: showing both masculine and feminine traits
definition: displaying traditionally masculine and traditionally feminine psychological characteristics.

plain_en: starvation diet despite being underweight
definition: an eating disorder in which a person (usually an adolescent female) maintains a starvation diet despite being significantly underweight, and has an inaccurate self-perception; sometimes accompanied by excessive exercise.

plain_en: molecule that blocks a neurotransmitter
definition: a molecule that inhibits or blocks a neurotransmitter's action.

plain_en: cannot form new memories
definition: an inability to form new memories.

plain_en: drugs that calm anxiety and agitation
definition: drugs used to control anxiety and agitation.

plain_en: drugs treating depression and related disorders
definition: drugs used to treat depressive disorders, anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive and related disorders, and posttraumatic stress disorder. (Several widely used antidepressant drugs are selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors - SSRIs.)

plain_en: drugs treating schizophrenia and severe thought disorders
definition: drugs used to treat schizophrenia and other forms of severe thought disorders.

plain_en: harmful, destructive behavior toward others
definition: negative, destructive, harmful behavior. The opposite of prosocial behavior.

plain_en: conscienceless, often aggressive or manipulative personality
definition: a personality disorder in which a person (usually a man) exhibits a lack of conscience for wrongdoing, even toward friends and family members; may be aggressive and ruthless or a clever con artist.

plain_en: disorders of excessive fear and anxiety
definition: a group of disorders characterized by excessive fear and anxiety and related maladaptive behaviors.

plain_en: language impairment from brain damage
definition: impairment of language, usually caused by left hemisphere damage either to Broca's area (impairing speaking) or to Wernicke's area (impairing understanding).

plain_en: urge to move toward or away from something
definition: the drive to move toward (approach) or away from (avoid) a stimulus.

plain_en: test predicting future performance ability
definition: a test designed to predict a person's future performance; aptitude is the capacity to learn.

plain_en: no sexual attraction to others
definition: having no sexual attraction toward others.

plain_en: fitting new experiences into existing schemas
definition: interpreting our new experiences in terms of our existing schemas.

plain_en: cortex areas for thinking, learning, and memory
definition: areas of the cerebral cortex that are not involved in primary motor or sensory functions; rather, they are involved in higher mental functions such as learning, remembering, thinking, and speaking.

plain_en: learning that events go together
definition: learning that certain events occur together. The events may be two stimuli (as in classical conditioning) or a response and its consequence (as in operant conditioning).

plain_en: emotional bond; child seeks closeness to caregiver
definition: an emotional tie with others; shown in young children by their seeking closeness to caregivers and showing distress on separation.

plain_en: disorder of inattention, hyperactivity, impulsivity
definition: a psychological disorder marked by extreme inattention and/or hyperactivity and impulsivity.

plain_en: feelings that predispose how we respond
definition: feelings, often influenced by our beliefs, that predispose us to respond in a particular way to objects, people, and events.

plain_en: explaining behavior by situation or personality
definition: the theory that we explain someone's behavior by crediting either the situation (a situational attribution) or the person's stable, enduring traits (a dispositional attribution).

plain_en: the sense of hearing
definition: the sense or act of hearing.

plain_en: childhood disorder of social and communication limits
definition: a disorder that appears in childhood and is marked by limitations in communication and social interaction, and by rigidly fixated interests and repetitive behaviors.

plain_en: still light seems to move in darkness
definition: the illusory movement of a still spot of light in a dark room.

plain_en: unconscious encoding of incidental, well-learned information
definition: unconscious encoding of incidental information, such as space, time, and frequency, and of familiar or well-learned information, such as sounds, smells, and word meanings.

plain_en: nervous system controlling glands and organ muscles
definition: the part of the peripheral nervous system that controls the glands and the muscles of the internal organs (such as the heart). Its sympathetic division arouses; its parasympathetic division calms.

plain_en: judging likelihood by what comes to mind easily
definition: judging the likelihood of events based on their availability in memory; if instances come readily to mind (perhaps because of their vividness), we presume such events are common.

plain_en: pairing unpleasant state with unwanted behavior
definition: associates an unpleasant state (such as nausea) with an unwanted behavior (such as drinking alcohol).

plain_en: long neuron branch sending messages outward
definition: the segmented neuron extension that passes messages through its branches to other neurons or to muscles or glands.

plain_en: infant makes speech-like sounds before real words
definition: the stage in speech development, beginning around 4 months, during which an infant spontaneously utters various sounds that are not all related to the household language.

plain_en: sedative drugs that calm but impair thinking
definition: drugs that depress central nervous system activity, reducing anxiety but impairing memory and judgment.

plain_en: energy burned while at rest
definition: the body's resting rate of energy output.

plain_en: infant's sense that world is safe
definition: according to Erik Erikson, a sense that the world is predictable and trustworthy; said to be formed during infancy by appropriate experiences with responsive caregivers.

plain_en: actions shape thoughts and feelings
definition: the tendency of behavior to influence our own and others' thoughts, feelings, and actions.

plain_en: study of genes versus environment on behavior
definition: the study of the relative power and limits of genetic and environmental influences on behavior.

plain_en: using learning principles to change behavior
definition: therapy that uses learning principles to reduce unwanted behaviors.

plain_en: personality shaped by learned habits
definition: focuses on the effects of learning on our personality development.

plain_en: psychology should study observable behavior only
definition: the view that psychology (1) should be an objective science that (2) studies behavior without reference to mental processes. Most research psychologists today agree with (1) but not with (2).

plain_en: clinging to beliefs after evidence fades
definition: the persistence of one's initial conceptions even after the basis on which they were formed has been discredited.

plain_en: five broad personality traits
definition: five traits -openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism -that describe personality. (Also called the five-factor model.)

plain_en: depth cue needing both eyes
definition: a depth cue, such as retinal disparity, that depends on the use of two eyes.

plain_en: study of body-brain links to behavior
definition: the scientific study of the links between biological (genetic, neural, hormonal) and psychological processes. (Some biological psychologists call themselves behavioral neuroscientists, neuropsychologists, behavior geneticists, physiological psychologists, or biopsychologists.)

plain_en: drugs or procedures acting on body
definition: prescribed medications or procedures that act directly on the person's physiology.

plain_en: combining biological, psychological, social perspectives
definition: an integrated approach that incorporates biological, psychological, and social-cultural levels of analysis.

plain_en: swings between depression and mania
definition: a group of disorders in which a person alternates between the hopelessness and lethargy of depression and the overexcited state of mania. (Formerly called manic-depressive disorder.)

plain_en: severe mania with depression
definition: the most severe form, in which people experience a euphoric, talkative, highly energetic, and overly ambitious state that lasts a week or longer.

plain_en: milder mania alternating with depression
definition: a less severe form of bipolar in which people move between depression and a milder hypomania.

plain_en: eye spot with no light receptors
definition: the point at which the optic nerve leaves the eye, creating a "blind" spot because no receptor cells are located there.

plain_en: responding to sight without seeing
definition: a condition in which a person can respond to a visual stimulus without consciously experiencing it.

plain_en: building perception from sensory details
definition: information processing that begins with the sensory receptors and works up to the brain's integration of sensory information.

plain_en: oldest brain part controlling survival functions
definition: the central core of the brain, beginning where the spinal cord swells as it enters the skull; the brainstem is responsible for automatic survival functions.

plain_en: positive emotions widen thinking and build skills
definition: proposes that positive emotions broaden our awareness, which over time helps us build novel and meaningful skills and resilience that improve well-being.

plain_en: brain area controlling speech muscles
definition: a frontal lobe brain area, usually in the left hemisphere, that helps control language expression by directing the muscle movements involved in speech.

plain_en: binge eating followed by purging
definition: an eating disorder in which a person's binge eating (usually of high-calorie foods) is followed by inappropriate weight-loss-promoting behavior, such as vomiting, laxative use, fasting, or excessive exercise.

plain_en: exhaustion from overwhelming work
definition: physical, emotional, or mental exhaustion, brought on by an overburdening workload, which may negatively impact motivation, performance, and attitude.

plain_en: less help given when others are present
definition: the tendency for any given bystander to be less likely to give aid if other bystanders are present.

plain_en: deep study of one person or group
definition: a non-experimental technique in which one individual or group is studied in depth in the hope of revealing universal principles.

plain_en: releasing anger to relieve aggression
definition: in psychology, the idea that "releasing" aggressive energy (through action or fantasy) relieves aggressive urges.

plain_en: intelligence from general plus specific abilities
definition: the theory that our intelligence is based on g as well as specific abilities, bridged by Gf and Gc.

plain_en: neuron part holding nucleus
definition: the part of a neuron that contains the nucleus; the cell's life-support center.

plain_en: memory manager coordinating short-term stores
definition: a memory component that coordinates the activities of the phonological loop and visuospatial sketchpad.

plain_en: brain and spinal cord
definition: the brain and spinal cord.

plain_en: persuasion through careful argument evaluation
definition: occurs when interested people's thinking is influenced by considering evidence and arguments.

plain_en: hindbrain structure for balance and coordination
definition: [sehr-uh-BELL-um] the hindbrain's "little brain" at the rear of the brainstem; its functions include processing sensory input, coordinating movement output and balance, and enabling nonverbal learning and memory.

plain_en: outer brain layer for complex processing
definition: the intricate fabric of interconnected neural cells covering the forebrain's cerebral hemispheres; the body's ultimate control and information-processing center.

plain_en: missing obvious environmental changes
definition: failing to notice changes in the environment; a form of inattentional blindness.

plain_en: schizophrenia with early onset and worsening course
definition: (also called process schizophrenia) a form of schizophrenia in which symptoms usually appear by late adolescence or early adulthood. As people age, psychotic episodes last longer and recovery periods shorten.

plain_en: grouping items into manageable units
definition: organizing items into familiar, manageable units; often occurs automatically.

plain_en: 24-hour biological body rhythms
definition: our biological clock; regular bodily rhythms (for example, of temperature and wakefulness) that occur on a 24-hour cycle.

plain_en: linking stimuli to produce learned responses
definition: a type of learning in which we link two or more stimuli; as a result, to illustrate with Pavlov's classic experiment, the first stimulus (a tone) comes to elicit behavior (drooling) in anticipation of the second stimulus (food).

plain_en: coiled fluid-filled inner ear sound structure
definition: [KOHK-lee-uh] a coiled, bony, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear; sound waves traveling through the cochlear fluid trigger nerve impulses.

plain_en: device stimulating auditory nerve with electrodes
definition: a device for converting sounds into electrical signals and stimulating the auditory nerve through electrodes threaded into the cochlea.

plain_en: mental activities of thinking and knowing
definition: all the mental activities associated with thinking, knowing, remembering, and communicating.

plain_en: we reduce discomfort from inconsistent thoughts
definition: the theory that we act to reduce the discomfort (dissonance) we feel when two of our thoughts (cognitions) are inconsistent. For example, when we become aware that our attitudes and our actions clash, we can reduce the resulting dissonance by changing our attitudes.

plain_en: acquiring mental information through observation or language
definition: the acquisition of mental information, whether by observing events, by watching others, or through language.

plain_en: mental picture of an environment's layout
definition: a mental representation of the layout of one's environment. For example, after exploring a maze, rats act as if they have learned a cognitive map of it.

plain_en: study of brain activity behind thinking
definition: the interdisciplinary study of the brain activity linked with cognition.

plain_en: therapy teaching more adaptive thinking patterns
definition: therapy that teaches people new, more adaptive ways of thinking; based on the assumption that thoughts intervene between events and our emotional reactions.

plain_en: therapy combining thinking and behavior changes
definition: a popular integrative therapy that combines cognitive therapy (changing self-defeating thinking) with behavior therapy (changing behavior).

plain_en: group sharing a common characteristic
definition: a group of people sharing a common characteristic, such as from a given time period.

plain_en: Jung's shared inherited memory reservoir
definition: Carl Jung's concept of a shared, inherited reservoir of memory traces from our species' history.

plain_en: culture prioritizing group goals over individual
definition: a cultural pattern that prioritizes the goals of important groups (often one's extended family or work group).

plain_en: seeing familiar objects as same color
definition: perceiving familiar objects as having consistent color, even if changing illumination alters the wavelengths reflected by the object.

plain_en: deep affection for those close to us
definition: the deep affectionate attachment we feel for those with whom our lives are intertwined.

plain_en: mental grouping of similar things
definition: a mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas, or people.

plain_en: stage of logical thinking about concrete events
definition: in Piaget's theory, the stage of cognitive development (from about 7 to 11 years of age) at which children can perform the mental operations that enable them to think logically about concrete (actual, physical) events.

plain_en: reinforcer learned through association with another
definition: a stimulus that gains its reinforcing power through its association with a primary reinforcer; also known as a secondary reinforcer.

plain_en: learned reaction to a conditioned stimulus
definition: in classical conditioning, a learned response to a previously neutral (but now conditioned) stimulus (CS).

plain_en: neutral stimulus that now triggers response
definition: in classical conditioning, an originally neutral stimulus that, after association with an unconditioned stimulus (UCS), comes to trigger a conditioned response (CR).

plain_en: hearing loss from damaged sound conduction
definition: a less common form of hearing loss, caused by damage to the mechanical system that conducts sound waves to the cochlea.

plain_en: retinal receptors for color and detail
definition: retinal receptors that are concentrated near the center of the retina and that function in daylight or in well-lit conditions. Cones detect fine detail and give rise to color sensations.

plain_en: seeking information that supports our beliefs
definition: a tendency to search for information that supports our preconceptions and to ignore or distort contradictory evidence.

plain_en: perceived incompatibility of actions or goals
definition: a perceived incompatibility of actions, goals, or ideas.

plain_en: adjusting behavior to match group standards
definition: adjusting our behavior or thinking to coincide with a group standard.

plain_en: extra factor that may affect results
definition: in an experiment, a factor other than the factor being studied that might influence a study's results.

plain_en: awareness of ourselves and environment
definition: our subjective awareness of ourselves and our environment.

plain_en: properties stay same despite form changes
definition: the principle (which Piaget believed to be a part of concrete operational reasoning) that properties such as mass, volume, and number remain the same despite changes in the forms of objects.

plain_en: how well a test measures a concept
definition: how much a test measures a concept or trait.

plain_en: how well a test samples relevant behavior
definition: the extent to which a test samples the behavior that is of interest.

plain_en: rewarding every correct response
definition: reinforcing the desired response every time it occurs.

plain_en: comparison group not receiving treatment
definition: in an experiment, the group not exposed to the treatment; contrasts with the experimental group and serves as a comparison for evaluating the effect of the treatment.

plain_en: depth cue from combining retinal images
definition: a cue to nearby objects' distance, enabled by the brain combining retinal images.

plain_en: narrowing options to one best answer
definition: narrowing the available problem solutions to determine the single best solution.

plain_en: reducing stress through emotional or behavioral methods
definition: alleviating stress using emotional, cognitive, or behavioral methods.

plain_en: eye's clear protective outer layer
definition: the eye's clear, protective outer layer, covering the pupil and iris.

plain_en: clogged heart vessels; leading cause of death
definition: the clogging of the vessels that nourish the heart muscle; the leading cause of death in many developed countries.

plain_en: fibers connecting the two brain hemispheres
definition: [KOR-pus kah-LOW-sum] the large band of neural fibers connecting the two brain hemispheres and carrying messages between them.

plain_en: how two things change together and predict each other
definition: a measure of the extent to which two factors vary together, and thus of how well either factor predicts the other.

plain_en: number showing strength of a relationship
definition: a statistical index of the relationship between two things (from −1.00 to +1.00).

plain_en: using conditioning to replace unwanted responses with new ones
definition: behavior therapy procedures that use classical conditioning to evoke new responses to stimuli that are triggering unwanted behaviors; include exposure therapies and aversive conditioning.

plain_en: making new and useful ideas
definition: the ability to produce new and valuable ideas.

plain_en: early window when experience must shape normal development
definition: an optimal period early in the life of an organism when exposure to certain stimuli or experiences produces normal development.

plain_en: questioning claims instead of accepting them automatically
definition: thinking that does not automatically accept arguments and conclusions. Rather, it examines assumptions, appraises the source, discerns hidden biases, evaluates evidence, and assesses conclusions.

plain_en: comparing different age groups at one time
definition: research that compares people of different ages at the same point in time.

plain_en: stored knowledge and verbal skills that grow with age
definition: our accumulated knowledge and verbal skills; tends to increase with age.

plain_en: computer-combined X-rays showing a brain slice
definition: a series of X-ray photographs taken from different angles and combined by computer into a composite representation of a slice of the brain's structure.
barron_kp: Computerized axial tomography (CAT or CT) scan

plain_en: shared behaviors and beliefs passed down generations
definition: the enduring behaviors, ideas, attitudes, values, and traditions shared by a group of people and transmitted from one generation to the next.

plain_en: explaining a study's purpose and deceptions afterward
definition: the postexperimental explanation of a study, including its purpose and any deceptions, to its participants.

plain_en: encoding by meaning, which aids later recall
definition: encoding semantically, based on the meaning of the words; tends to yield the best retention.

plain_en: unconscious distortions that reduce anxiety
definition: in psychoanalytic theory, the ego's protective methods of reducing anxiety by unconsciously distorting reality.

plain_en: losing self-awareness and restraint in anonymous groups
definition: the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint occurring in group situations that foster arousal and anonymity.

plain_en: moving people with disorders out of institutions
definition: the process, begun in the late twentieth century, of moving people with psychological disorders out of institutional facilities.

plain_en: false feeling that this has happened before
definition: that eerie sense that "I've experienced this before." Cues from the current situation may unconsciously trigger retrieval of an earlier experience.

plain_en: large slow waves of deep sleep
definition: the large, slow brain waves associated with deep sleep.

plain_en: false belief, often of persecution or grandeur
definition: a false belief, often of persecution or grandeur, that may accompany psychotic disorders.

plain_en: branching neuron parts that receive messages
definition: a neuron's often bushy, branching extensions that receive and integrate messages, conducting impulses toward the cell body.

plain_en: the measured outcome in an experiment
definition: in an experiment, the outcome that is measured; the variable that may change when the independent variable is manipulated.

plain_en: drugs that slow neural activity and body functions
definition: drugs that reduce neural activity and slow body functions.

plain_en: disorders marked by lasting sad or empty mood
definition: a group of disorders characterized by an enduring sad, empty, or irritable mood, along with physical and cognitive changes that affect a person's ability to function.

plain_en: seeing in three dimensions and judging distance
definition: the ability to see objects in three dimensions although the images that strike the retina are two-dimensional; allows us to judge distance.

plain_en: numbers summarizing a group's characteristics
definition: numerical data used to measure and describe characteristics of groups; include measures of central tendency and measures of variation.

plain_en: study of change across the lifespan
definition: a branch of psychology that studies physical, cognitive, and social change throughout the lifespan.

plain_en: genetic vulnerability plus stress causes disorder
definition: the concept that genetic predispositions (diathesis) combine with environmental stressors (stress) to influence psychological disorder.

plain_en: smallest detectable difference between two stimuli
definition: the minimum difference between two stimuli required for detection 50 percent of the time. We experience the difference threshold as a just noticeable difference (or jnd).

plain_en: learning to tell a conditioned stimulus from others
definition: in classical conditioning, the learned ability to distinguish between a conditioned stimulus and other stimuli that have not been associated with a conditioned stimulus. (In operant conditioning, the ability to distinguish responses that are reinforced from similar responses that are not reinforced.)

plain_en: unfair negative behavior toward a group
definition: in social psychology, unjustifiable negative behavior toward a group or its members.

plain_en: signal that a response will be reinforced
definition: in operant conditioning, a stimulus that elicits a response after association with reinforcement (in contrast to related stimuli not associated with reinforcement).

plain_en: split consciousness letting thoughts and actions run separately
definition: a split in consciousness, which allows some thoughts and behaviors to occur simultaneously with others.

plain_en: memory gaps, often after trauma
definition: a disorder in which people with intact brains reportedly experience memory gaps; people with dissociative amnesia may report not remembering trauma-related specific events, people, places, or aspects of their identity and life history.

plain_en: disrupted integration of consciousness, memory, or identity
definition: a controversial, rare group of disorders characterized by a disruption of or discontinuity in the normal integration of consciousness, memory, identity, emotion, perception, body representation, motor control, and behavior.

plain_en: two or more alternating personalities in one person
definition: a rare dissociative disorder in which a person exhibits two or more distinct and alternating personalities. (Formerly called multiple personality disorder.)

plain_en: generating many possible solutions
definition: expanding the number of possible problem solutions; creative thinking that diverges in different directions.

plain_en: neither participants nor staff know who got treatment
definition: an experimental procedure in which both the research participants and the research staff are ignorant (blind) about whether the research participants have received the treatment or a placebo. Commonly used in drug-evaluation studies.

plain_en: images and thoughts during sleep
definition: a sequence of images, emotions, and thoughts passing through a sleeping person's mind.

plain_en: bodily need creates drive to satisfy it
definition: the idea that a physiological need creates an aroused state (a drive) that motivates an organism to satisfy the need.

plain_en: manual for classifying mental disorders
definition: the American Psychiatric Association's Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition, Text Revision; a widely used system for classifying psychological disorders.

plain_en: processing on conscious and unconscious tracks at once
definition: the principle that information is often simultaneously processed on separate conscious and unconscious tracks.

plain_en: brief memory of sounds just heard
definition: a momentary sensory memory of auditory stimuli; if attention is elsewhere, sounds and words can still be recalled within 3 or 4 seconds.

plain_en: therapy mixing techniques from different approaches
definition: an approach to psychotherapy that uses techniques from various forms of therapy.

plain_en: development shaped by nested layers of environment
definition: a theory of the social environment's influence on human development, using five nested systems (microsystem; mesosystem; exosystem; macrosystem; chronosystem) ranging from direct to indirect influences.

plain_en: recording of brain's electrical waves via scalp electrodes
definition: an amplified recording of the waves of electrical activity sweeping across the brain's surface. These waves are measured by electrodes placed on the scalp.

plain_en: strength of relationship between two variables
definition: the strength of the relationship between two variables. The larger the effect size, the more one variable can be explained by the other.

plain_en: encoding requiring attention and conscious effort
definition: encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.

plain_en: Freud's executive mediator among id, superego, reality
definition: the partly conscious, "executive" part of personality that, according to Freud, mediates among the demands of the id, the superego, and reality. The ego operates on the reality principle, satisfying the id's desires in ways that will realistically bring pleasure rather than pain.

plain_en: child's difficulty seeing another's viewpoint
definition: in Piaget's theory, the preoperational child's difficulty taking another's point of view.

plain_en: brief electric current to brain for severe depression
definition: a biomedical therapy for severe depression in which a brief electric current is sent through the brain of an anesthetized person.

plain_en: body states influence thinking and judgments
definition: the influence of bodily sensations, gestures, and other states on cognitive preferences and judgments.

plain_en: ages 18 to mid-twenties, not yet fully adult
definition: a period from about age 18 to the mid-twenties, when many persons in Western cultures are no longer adolescents but have not yet achieved full independence as adults.

plain_en: whole-organism response: arousal, expression, interpretation
definition: a response of the whole organism, involving (1) physiological arousal, (2) expressive behaviors, and, most importantly, (3) conscious experience resulting from one's interpretations.

plain_en: coping by easing emotions, avoiding the stressor
definition: attempting to alleviate stress by avoiding or ignoring a stressor and attending to emotional needs related to our stress reaction.

plain_en: ability to perceive, understand, manage, use emotions
definition: the ability to perceive, understand, manage, and use emotions.

plain_en: test built from items distinguishing groups
definition: a test (such as the MMPI) created by selecting from a pool of items those that discriminate between groups.

plain_en: getting information into memory
definition: the process of getting information into the memory system -for example, by extracting meaning.

plain_en: memory-specific cues and contexts aid recall
definition: the idea that cues and contexts specific to a particular memory will be most effective in helping us recall it.

plain_en: slow chemical communication via hormones in blood
definition: the body's "slow" chemical communication system; a set of glands and fat tissue that secrete hormones into the bloodstream.

plain_en: natural opioid-like neurotransmitters for pain and pleasure
definition: [en-DOR-fins] "morphine within" -natural, opioid-like neurotransmitters linked to pain control and to pleasure.

plain_en: all nongenetic influences on us
definition: every nongenetic influence, from prenatal nutrition to our experiences of the people and things around us.

plain_en: how environments affect gene expression without DNA change
definition: "above" or "in addition to" (epi) genetics; the study of the molecular mechanisms by which environments can influence genetic expression (without a DNA change).

plain_en: conscious memory of personally experienced events
definition: explicit memory of personally experienced events; one of our two conscious memory systems (the other is semantic memory).

plain_en: relationship give-and-take proportional for both
definition: a condition in which people receive from a relationship in proportion to what they give to it.

plain_en: female sex hormones secreted more by females
definition: sex hormones, such as estradiol, that contribute to female sex characteristics and are secreted in greater amounts by females than by males.

plain_en: clinical decisions integrating research, expertise, patient preferences
definition: clinical decision making that integrates the best available research with clinical expertise and patient characteristics and preferences.

plain_en: study of behavior and mind via natural selection
definition: the study of the evolution of behavior and the mind, using principles of natural selection.

plain_en: cognitive skills for planning and goal-directed behavior
definition: cognitive skills that work together, enabling us to generate, organize, plan, and implement goal-directed behavior.

plain_en: manipulating variables to observe effects, with random assignment
definition: a research method in which an investigator manipulates one or more factors (independent variables) to observe the effect on some behavior or mental process (the dependent variable). By random assignment of participants, the experimenter aims to control other relevant factors.

plain_en: group exposed to the treatment
definition: in an experiment, the group exposed to the treatment, that is, to one version of the independent variable.

plain_en: researchers unintentionally swaying results toward beliefs
definition: bias caused when researchers may unintentionally influence results to confirm their own beliefs.

plain_en: consciously known and declared facts and experiences
definition: retention of facts and experiences that we can consciously know and "declare." (Also called declarative memory.)

plain_en: behavioral techniques exposing people to feared things
definition: behavioral techniques, such as systematic desensitization and virtual reality exposure therapy, that treat anxieties by exposing people (in imaginary or actual situations) to the things they fear and avoid.

plain_en: belief that outside forces control our fate
definition: the perception that outside forces beyond our personal control determine our fate.

plain_en: diminishing of conditioned response without reinforcement
definition: in classical conditioning, the diminishing of a conditioned response when an unconditioned stimulus does not follow a conditioned stimulus. (In operant conditioning, when a response is no longer reinforced.)

plain_en: performing behavior for rewards or to avoid punishment
definition: the desire to perform a behavior to receive promised rewards or avoid threatened punishment.

plain_en: facial muscle states trigger matching feelings
definition: the tendency of facial muscle states to trigger corresponding feelings such as fear, anger, or happiness.

plain_en: statistical method identifying clusters of related test items
definition: a statistical procedure that identifies clusters of related items (called factors) on a test; used to identify different dimensions of performance that underlie a person's total score.

plain_en: can be disproven by observation or experiment
definition: the possibility that an idea, hypothesis, or theory can be disproven by observation or experiment.

plain_en: therapy treating people within their family system
definition: therapy that treats people in the context of their family system. Views an individual's unwanted behaviors as influenced by, or directed at, other family members.

plain_en: brain cells tuned to specific visual features
definition: nerve cells in the brain's visual cortex that respond to specific features of the stimulus, such as shape, angle, or movement.

plain_en: disordered eating that harms health or mind
definition: a group of disorders characterized by altered consumption or absorption of food that impairs health or psychological functioning. (Feeding disorders typically occur in infants and young children, whereas eating disorders affect people who self-feed.)

plain_en: good mood makes people more helpful
definition: people's tendency to be helpful when in a good mood.

plain_en: birth defects from mother's heavy drinking
definition: physical and cognitive function deficits in children caused by their birth mother's heavy drinking during pregnancy. In severe cases, symptoms include a small, out-of-proportion head and distinct facial features.

plain_en: separating main objects from background
definition: the organization of the visual field into objects (the figures) that stand out from their surroundings (the ground).

plain_en: stuck seeing a problem one way
definition: in cognition, the inability to see a problem from a new perspective; an obstacle to problem solving.

plain_en: belief that abilities cannot be changed
definition: the view that intelligence, abilities, and talents are unchangeable, even with effort.

plain_en: reward after a set amount of time
definition: in operant conditioning, a reinforcement schedule that reinforces a response only after a specified time has elapsed.

plain_en: reward after a set number of responses
definition: in operant conditioning, a reinforcement schedule that reinforces a response only after a specified number of responses.

plain_en: vivid memory of an emotional event
definition: a clear memory of an emotionally significant moment or event.

plain_en: total absorption with lost sense of time
definition: a completely involved, focused state, with diminished awareness of self and time; results from full engagement of our skills.

plain_en: fast abstract reasoning that declines with age
definition: our ability to reason speedily and abstractly; tends to decrease with age, especially during late adulthood.

plain_en: IQ scores rising over generations
definition: the rise in intelligence test performance over time and across cultures.

plain_en: scan showing brain activity via blood flow
definition: a technique for revealing blood flow and, therefore, brain activity by comparing successive MRI scans. fMRI scans show brain function as well as structure.

plain_en: small favor first, then bigger compliance
definition: the tendency for people who have first agreed to a small request to comply later with a larger request.

plain_en: front brain region for complex thinking
definition: consists of the cerebral cortex, thalamus, and hypothalamus; manages complex cognitive activities, sensory and associative functions, and voluntary motor activities.

plain_en: stage of abstract logical thinking, from age 12
definition: in Piaget's theory, the stage of cognitive development (normally beginning about age 12) at which people begin to think logically about abstract concepts.

plain_en: retina center packed with cones
definition: the central focal point in the retina, around which the eye's cones cluster.

plain_en: how a question is worded shapes choices
definition: the way an issue is posed; how an issue is framed can significantly affect decisions and judgments.

plain_en: twins from two eggs, like ordinary siblings
definition: individuals who developed from separate fertilized eggs. They are genetically no closer than ordinary siblings, but they share a prenatal environment.

plain_en: saying whatever comes to mind freely
definition: in psychoanalysis, a method of exploring the unconscious in which the person relaxes and says whatever comes to mind, no matter how trivial or embarrassing.

plain_en: number of wave cycles per second
definition: the number of complete wavelengths that pass a point in a given time (for example, per second).

plain_en: pitch sensed from nerve impulse rate
definition: in hearing, the theory that the rate of nerve impulses traveling up the auditory nerve matches the frequency of a tone, thus enabling us to sense its pitch. (Also called temporal coding.)

plain_en: front cortex for movement, language, planning
definition: the portion of the cerebral cortex lying just behind the forehead. They enable linguistic processing, muscle movements, higher-order thinking, and executive functioning (such as making plans and judgments).

plain_en: blocked goals breed anger and aggression
definition: the principle that frustration -the blocking of an attempt to achieve some goal -creates anger, which can generate aggression.

plain_en: blaming people, ignoring situations
definition: the tendency for observers, when analyzing others' behavior, to underestimate the impact of the situation and to overestimate the impact of personal disposition.

plain_en: spinal cord gate controls pain signals
definition: the theory that the spinal cord contains a neurological "gate" that blocks pain signals or allows them to pass on to the brain. The "gate" is opened by the activity of pain signals traveling up small nerve fibers and is closed by activity in larger fibers or by information coming from the brain.

plain_en: cultural traits tied to biological sex
definition: in psychology, the attitudes, feelings, and behaviors that a given culture associates with a person's biological sex. (See also gender identity.)

plain_en: personal sense of being male or female
definition: our personal sense of being male, female, neither, or some combination of male and female, regardless of whether this identity matches our sex assigned at birth, and the social affiliation that may result from this identity.

plain_en: expected behaviors for men and women
definition: a set of expected behaviors, attitudes, and traits for men and for women.

plain_en: taking on traditional masculine or feminine roles
definition: the acquisition of a traditional masculine or feminine role.

plain_en: body's three-stage stress response
definition: Selye's concept of the body's adaptive response to stress in three phases -alarm, resistance, exhaustion.

plain_en: one general ability behind all mental tasks
definition: according to Spearman and others, underlies all mental abilities and is therefore measured by every task on an intelligence test.

plain_en: similar stimuli trigger the learned response
definition: (also called stimulus generalization) in classical conditioning, the tendency, once a response has been conditioned, for stimuli similar to the conditioned stimulus to elicit similar responses. (In operant conditioning, when responses learned in one situation occur in other, similar situations.)

plain_en: constant tense, worried arousal
definition: an anxiety disorder in which a person is continually tense, apprehensive, and in a state of autonomic nervous system arousal.

plain_en: basic units of heredity
definition: the biochemical units of heredity.

plain_en: complete genetic instructions for an organism
definition: the complete instructions for making an organism.

plain_en: organized whole; we perceive wholes
definition: an organized whole. Gestalt psychologists emphasized our tendency to integrate pieces of information into meaningful wholes.

plain_en: cells that support and protect neurons
definition: cells in the nervous system that support, nourish, and protect neurons; they may also play a role in learning, thinking, and memory.

plain_en: blood sugar that fuels body tissues
definition: the form of sugar that circulates in the blood and provides the major source of energy for body tissues. When its level is low, we feel hunger.

plain_en: rules for communicating and understanding language
definition: in a language, a system of rules that enables us to communicate with and understand others. Semantics is the language's set of rules for deriving meaning from sounds, and syntax is its set of rules for combining words into grammatically sensible sentences.

plain_en: thankful feeling for benefits received or good fortune
definition: an appreciative emotion people often experience when they benefit from other's actions or recognize their own good fortune.

plain_en: passion and persistence toward long-term goals
definition: in psychology, passion and perseverance in the pursuit of long-term goals.

plain_en: gradual mutual steps to ease international tensions
definition: Graduated and Reciprocated Initiatives in Tension-Reduction -a strategy designed to decrease international tensions.

plain_en: group discussion strengthens shared inclinations
definition: the enhancement of a group's prevailing inclinations through discussion within the group.

plain_en: therapy done with groups, not individuals
definition: therapy conducted with groups rather than individuals, providing benefits from group interaction.

plain_en: perceiving stimuli as organized coherent groups
definition: the perceptual tendency to organize stimuli into coherent groups.

plain_en: harmony desire overrides realistic evaluation of options
definition: the mode of thinking that occurs when the desire for harmony in a decision-making group overrides a realistic appraisal of alternatives.

plain_en: focus on learning rather than fixed ability
definition: a focus on learning and growing rather than viewing abilities as fixed.

plain_en: the sense of taste
definition: our sense of taste.

plain_en: less responsiveness after repeated stimulation
definition: decreasing responsiveness with repeated stimulation. As infants gain familiarity with repeated exposure to a stimulus, their interest wanes and they look away sooner.

plain_en: false sensory experiences without external stimuli
definition: false sensory experiences, such as seeing something in the absence of an external visual stimulus.

plain_en: drugs that distort perception and evoke sensory images
definition: psychedelic ("mind-manifesting") drugs that distort perceptions and evoke sensory images in the absence of sensory input.

plain_en: studies psychological and behavioral influences on health
definition: a subfield of psychology that explores the impact of psychological, behavioral, and cultural factors on health and wellness.

plain_en: genetic transmission of traits from parents
definition: the genetic transfer of characteristics from parents to offspring.

plain_en: mental shortcut for quick, error-prone judgments
definition: a simple thinking strategy -a mental shortcut -that often allows us to make judgments and solve problems efficiently; usually speedier but also more error-prone than an algorithm.

plain_en: Maslow's pyramid of human needs, base first
definition: Maslow's levels of human needs, beginning at the base with physiological need. Often visualized as a pyramid, with needs nearer the base taking priority until they are satisfied.

plain_en: new neutral stimulus paired with conditioned stimulus
definition: a procedure in which the conditioned stimulus in one conditioning experience is paired with a new neutral stimulus, creating a second (often weaker) conditioned stimulus. For example, an animal that has learned that a tone predicts food might then learn that a light predicts the tone and begin responding to the light alone. (Also called second-order conditioning.)

plain_en: medulla, pons, cerebellum; basic survival and coordination
definition: consists of the medulla, pons, and cerebellum; directs essential survival functions, such as breathing, sleeping, and wakefulness, as well as coordination and balance.

plain_en: believing you'd have foreseen an outcome
definition: the tendency to believe, after learning an outcome, that one would have foreseen it. (Also known as the I-knew-it-all-along phenomenon.)

plain_en: brain structure processing explicit memories for storage
definition: a neural center located in the limbic system; helps process explicit (conscious) memories -of facts and events -for storage.

plain_en: bar graph showing a frequency distribution
definition: a bar graph depicting a frequency distribution.

plain_en: persistent difficulty discarding possessions
definition: a persistent difficulty parting with possessions, regardless of their value.

plain_en: maintaining balanced internal state
definition: a tendency to maintain a balanced or constant internal state; the regulation of any aspect of body chemistry, such as blood glucose, around a particular level.

plain_en: endocrine chemical messengers traveling through bloodstream
definition: chemical messengers that are manufactured by the endocrine glands, travel through the bloodstream, and affect other tissues.

plain_en: color dimension determined by light wavelength
definition: the dimension of color that is determined by the wavelength of light; what we know as the color names blue, green, and so forth.

plain_en: studies people-machine interaction and safe design
definition: a field of psychology allied with I/O psychology that explores how people and machines interact and how machines and physical environments can be made safe and easy to use.

plain_en: personality theories emphasizing healthy personal growth
definition: theories that view personality with a focus on the potential for healthy personal growth.

plain_en: bizarre sensations while falling asleep
definition: bizarre experiences, such as jerking or a feeling of falling or floating weightlessly, while transitioning to sleep. (Also called hypnic sensations.)

plain_en: suggestion that perceptions or behaviors will occur
definition: a social interaction in which one person (the hypnotist) suggests to another (the subject) that certain perceptions, feelings, thoughts, or behaviors will spontaneously occur; in a therapeutic context, the hypnotist attempts to use suggestion to reduce unpleasant physical sensations or emotions.

plain_en: directs eating, drinking, temperature; links emotion and reward
definition: [hi-po-THAL-uh-muss] a limbic system neural structure lying below (hypo) the thalamus; it directs several maintenance activities (eating, drinking, body temperature), helps govern the endocrine system, and is linked to emotion and reward.

plain_en: testable prediction often implied by a theory
definition: a testable prediction, often implied by a theory.

plain_en: brief visual sensory memory lasting fractions of a second
definition: a momentary sensory memory of visual stimuli; a photographic or picture-image memory lasting no more than a few tenths of a second.

plain_en: unconscious energy demanding immediate gratification
definition: a reservoir of unconscious psychic energy that, according to Freud, strives to satisfy basic sexual and aggressive drives. The id operates on the pleasure principle, demanding immediate gratification.

plain_en: twins from one fertilized egg, genetically identical
definition: individuals who developed from a single fertilized egg that split in two, creating two genetically identical organisms.

plain_en: our sense of self
definition: our sense of self; according to Erikson, the adolescent's task is to solidify a sense of self by testing and integrating various roles.

plain_en: perceiving a relationship that isn't there
definition: perceiving a relationship where none exists, or perceiving a stronger-than-actual relationship.

plain_en: skills and conditioned associations without conscious recall
definition: retention of learned skills or classically conditioned associations independent of conscious recollection. (Also called nondeclarative memory.)

plain_en: early-life strong attachment formation in animals
definition: the process by which certain animals form strong attachments during early life.

plain_en: missing visible objects when attention is elsewhere
definition: failing to see visible objects when our attention is directed elsewhere.

plain_en: reward or punishment that drives behavior
definition: a positive or negative environmental stimulus that motivates behavior.

plain_en: the factor researchers change and test
definition: in an experiment, the factor that is manipulated; the variable whose effect is being studied.

plain_en: prioritizing personal goals over group goals
definition: a cultural pattern that emphasizes people's own goals over group goals and defines identity mainly in terms of unique personal attributes.

plain_en: applying psychology to workplace behavior
definition: the application of psychological concepts and methods to optimizing human behavior in workplaces.

plain_en: data used to generalize from samples
definition: numerical data that allow one to generalize -to infer from sample data the probability of something being true of a population.

plain_en: accepting others' views about reality
definition: influence resulting from a person's willingness to accept others' opinions about reality.

plain_en: telling participants enough to choose participation
definition: giving potential participants enough information about a study to enable them to choose whether they wish to participate.

plain_en: the group we belong to
definition: "us" -people with whom we share a common identity.

plain_en: favoring our own group
definition: the tendency to favor our own group.

plain_en: innermost ear with cochlea and canals
definition: the innermost part of the ear, containing the cochlea, semicircular canals, and vestibular sacs.

plain_en: clinging or avoidant infant attachment style
definition: demonstrated by infants who display either a clinging, anxious attachment or an avoidant attachment that resists closeness.

plain_en: sudden realization of a solution
definition: a sudden realization of a problem's solution; contrasts with strategy-based solutions.

plain_en: solving problems by sudden realization
definition: solving problems through sudden insight; contrasts with strategy-based solutions.

plain_en: therapy raising awareness of hidden motives
definition: therapies that aim to improve psychological functioning by increasing a person's awareness of underlying motives and defenses.

plain_en: ongoing trouble falling or staying asleep
definition: recurring problems in falling or staying asleep.

plain_en: unlearned, fixed species-wide behavior pattern
definition: a complex behavior that is rigidly patterned throughout a species and is unlearned. instinctive drift the tendency of learned behavior to gradually revert to biologically predisposed patterns.

plain_en: learned behavior reverting to instinct
definition: the tendency of learned behavior to gradually revert to biologically predisposed patterns.

plain_en: ability to learn, solve problems, adapt
definition: the ability to learn from experience, solve problems, and use knowledge to adapt to new situations.

plain_en: score comparing mental age to actual age
definition: defined originally as the ratio of mental age (ma) to chronological age (ca) multiplied by 100 (thus, IQ = ma/ca × 100). On contemporary intelligence tests, the average performance for a given age is assigned a score of 100.

plain_en: test measuring mental abilities with scores
definition: a method for assessing an individual's mental aptitudes and comparing them with those of others, using numerical scores.

plain_en: wave energy affecting brightness or loudness
definition: the amount of energy in a light wave or sound wave, which influences what we perceive as brightness or loudness. Intensity is determined by the wave's amplitude (height).

plain_en: one factor's effect depends on another
definition: the interplay that occurs when the effect of one factor (such as environment) depends on another factor (such as heredity).

plain_en: mixing different topics during study
definition: a retrieval practice strategy that involves mixing the study of different topics.

plain_en: belief that we control our fate
definition: the perception that we control our own fate.

plain_en: neurons in brain and spinal cord
definition: neurons within the brain and spinal cord; they communicate internally and process information between the sensory inputs and motor outputs.

plain_en: noting hidden meanings to promote insight
definition: in psychoanalysis, the analyst's noting of supposed dream meanings, resistances, and other significant behaviors and events in order to promote insight.

plain_en: having both male and female characteristics
definition: possessing male and female biological sexual characteristics at birth.

plain_en: forming close, loving relationships
definition: in Erikson's theory, the ability to form close, loving relationships; a primary developmental task in young adulthood.

plain_en: doing something for its own sake
definition: the desire to perform a behavior effectively for its own sake.

plain_en: immediate automatic feeling without reasoning
definition: an effortless, immediate, automatic feeling or thought, as contrasted with explicit, conscious reasoning.

plain_en: colored eye muscle controlling pupil size
definition: a ring of muscle tissue that forms the colored portion of the eye around the pupil and controls the size of the pupil opening.

plain_en: belief people get what they deserve
definition: the tendency for people to believe the world is just and that people therefore get what they deserve and deserve what they get.

plain_en: sense of body position and movement
definition: [kin-ehs-THEE-sis] our movement sense -our system for sensing the position and movement of individual body parts.

plain_en: agreed systems of words for communication
definition: our agreed-upon systems of spoken, written, or signed words and the ways we combine them to communicate meaning.

plain_en: hidden learning shown only when rewarded
definition: learning that occurs but is not apparent until there is an incentive to demonstrate it.

plain_en: rewarded behaviors become more likely
definition: Thorndike's principle that behaviors followed by favorable (or reinforcing) consequences become more likely, and that behaviors followed by unfavorable (or punishing) consequences become less likely.

plain_en: ability to motivate and influence others
definition: an individual's ability to motivate and influence others to contribute to their group's success.

plain_en: passive resignation after unavoidable bad events
definition: the hopelessness and passive resignation humans and other animals learn when unable to avoid repeated aversive events.

plain_en: gaining new information or behaviors through experience
definition: the process of acquiring through experience new and relatively enduring information or behaviors.

plain_en: eye structure that focuses images
definition: the transparent structure behind the pupil that changes shape to help focus images on the retina.

plain_en: damage to brain tissue
definition: [LEE-zhuhn] tissue destruction. Brain lesions may occur naturally (from disease or trauma), during surgery, or experimentally (using electrodes to destroy brain cells).

plain_en: complementary biological to social views of a phenomenon
definition: the differing complementary views, from biological to psychological to social-cultural, for analyzing any given phenomenon.

plain_en: forebrain system linked to emotions and drives
definition: neural system located mostly in the forebrain -below the cerebral hemispheres -that includes the amygdala, hypothalamus, hippocampus, thalamus, and pituitary gland; associated with emotions and drives.

plain_en: language determines thought
definition: Whorf's hypothesis that language determines the way we think.

plain_en: language influences thought
definition: the idea that language influences the way we think.

plain_en: old surgery cutting frontal lobe connections to calm patients
definition: a psychosurgical procedure once used to calm uncontrollably emotional or violent patients. The procedure cut the nerves connecting the frontal lobes to the emotion-controlling centers of the inner brain.

plain_en: permanent, limitless store of knowledge and skills
definition: the relatively permanent and limitless archive of the memory system. Includes knowledge, skills, and experiences.

plain_en: strengthened neural firing after rapid stimulation; aids learning
definition: an increase in a nerve cell's firing potential after brief, rapid stimulation; a neural basis for learning and memory.

plain_en: research following and retesting the same people over time
definition: research that follows and retests the same people over time.

plain_en: place with flexible, informal norms
definition: a place with flexible and informal norms.

plain_en: two-plus weeks of depressed mood or lost interest
definition: a disorder in which a person experiences five or more symptoms lasting two or more weeks, in the absence of drug use or a medical condition, at least one of which must be either (1) depressed mood or (2) loss of interest or pleasure.

plain_en: hyperactive, wildly optimistic state with poor judgment
definition: a hyperactive, wildly optimistic state in which dangerously poor judgment is common.

plain_en: biological growth enabling orderly behavior changes
definition: biological growth processes that enable orderly changes in behavior, relatively uninfluenced by experience.

plain_en: arithmetic average of scores
definition: the arithmetic average of a distribution, obtained by adding the scores and then dividing by the number of scores.

plain_en: middle score in a distribution
definition: the middle score in a distribution; half the scores are above it and half are below it.

plain_en: psychological disorders have physical causes, diagnosable and treatable
definition: the concept that diseases, in this case psychological disorders, have physical causes that can be diagnosed, treated, and, in most cases, cured, often through treatment in a hospital.

plain_en: brainstem base controlling heartbeat and breathing
definition: [muh-DUL-uh] the hindbrain structure that is the brainstem's base; controls heartbeat and breathing.

plain_en: imaging measuring brain's magnetic fields
definition: a brain-imaging technique that measures magnetic fields from the brain's natural electrical activity.

plain_en: persistence of learning via encoding, storage, retrieval
definition: the persistence of learning over time through the encoding, storage, and retrieval of information.

plain_en: neural storage of a long-term memory
definition: the neural storage of a long-term memory.

plain_en: first menstrual period
definition: [meh-NAR-key] the first menstrual period.

plain_en: natural end of menstruation and reproduction decline
definition: the time of natural cessation of menstruation; also refers to the biological changes a woman experiences as her ability to reproduce declines.

plain_en: performance level typical of a given age
definition: a measure of intelligence test performance devised by Binet; the level of performance typically associated with children of a certain chronological age. Thus, a child who does as well as an average 8-year-old is said to have a mental age of 8.

plain_en: tendency to approach problems one familiar way
definition: a tendency to approach a problem in one particular way, often a way that has been successful in the past.

plain_en: repeated exposure increases liking
definition: the tendency for repeated exposure to novel stimuli to increase our liking of them.

plain_en: statistical combining of multiple study results
definition: a statistical procedure for analyzing the results of multiple studies to reach an overall conclusion.

plain_en: thinking about and evaluating our own thinking
definition: cognition about our cognition; keeping track of and evaluating our mental processes.

plain_en: brainstem-top region linking hindbrain and forebrain
definition: found atop the brainstem; connects the hindbrain with the forebrain, controls some motor movement, and transmits auditory and visual information.

plain_en: chamber with three tiny bones concentrating eardrum vibrations
definition: the chamber between the eardrum and cochlea containing three tiny bones that concentrate the vibrations of the eardrum on the cochlea's oval window.

plain_en: attending to present experience nonjudgmentally
definition: a reflective practice in which people attend to current experiences in a nonjudgmental and accepting manner.

plain_en: widely used personality test originally for emotional disorders
definition: the most widely researched and clinically used of all personality tests. Originally developed to identify emotional disorders (still considered its most appropriate use), this test is now used for many other screening purposes.

plain_en: neurons firing when acting or observing actions
definition: neurons that some scientists believe fire when we perform certain actions or observe another doing so. The brain's mirroring of another's action may enable imitation and empathy.

plain_en: conflicting sides each see themselves as good, other as evil
definition: mutual views often held by conflicting parties, as when each side sees itself as ethical and peaceful and views the other side as evil and aggressive.

plain_en: misleading information corrupts memory
definition: occurs when a memory has been corrupted by misleading information.

plain_en: memory aids using imagery and organization
definition: [nih-MON-iks] memory aids, especially those techniques that use vivid imagery and organizational devices.

plain_en: most frequently occurring score
definition: the most frequently occurring score(s) in a distribution.

plain_en: observing and imitating a behavior
definition: the process of observing and imitating a specific behavior.

plain_en: depth cue usable by one eye alone
definition: a depth cue, such as interposition or linear perspective, available to either eye alone.

plain_en: recalling memories matching current mood
definition: the tendency to recall experiences that are consistent with one's current good or bad mood.

plain_en: smallest meaningful language unit
definition: in a language, the smallest unit that carries meaning; may be a word or a part of a word (such as a prefix).

plain_en: inner drive that starts and guides actions
definition: a need or desire that energizes and directs behavior.

plain_en: neurons sending signals out from brain and spinal cord
definition: neurons that carry outgoing information from the brain and spinal cord to the muscles and glands.

plain_en: brain area controlling voluntary body movements
definition: a cerebral cortex area at the rear of the frontal lobes that controls voluntary movements.

plain_en: magnetic scan showing soft tissue and brain structure
definition: a technique that uses magnetic fields and radio waves to produce computer-generated images of soft tissue. MRI scans show brain anatomy.

plain_en: random gene-copying error causing a change
definition: a random error in gene replication that leads to a change.

plain_en: fatty coating that speeds up neuron signals
definition: a fatty tissue layer segmentally encasing the axons of some neurons; it enables vastly greater transmission speed as neural impulses hop from one node to the next.

plain_en: excessive love of oneself and self-focus
definition: excessive self-love and self-absorption.

plain_en: sudden uncontrollable sleep attacks, often into REM
definition: a sleep disorder characterized by uncontrollable sleep attacks. The affected person may lapse directly into REM sleep, often at inopportune times.

plain_en: inherited helpful traits get passed to offspring
definition: the principle that the inherited traits enabling an organism to survive and reproduce in a particular environment will (in competition with other trait variations) most likely be passed on to succeeding generations.

plain_en: watching behavior in real settings without interference
definition: a non-experimental technique of observing and recording behavior in naturally occurring situations without trying to manipulate and control the situation.

plain_en: debate over genes versus experience shaping traits
definition: the longstanding controversy over the relative contributions that genes and experience make to the development of psychological traits and behaviors. Today's science views traits and behaviors as arising from the interaction of nature and nurture.

plain_en: altered awareness reported after nearly dying
definition: an altered state of consciousness reported after a close brush with death (such as cardiac arrest); often similar to drug-induced hallucinations.

plain_en: strengthening behavior by removing something unpleasant
definition: increasing behaviors by stopping or reducing an aversive stimulus. A negative reinforcer is any stimulus that, when removed after a response, strengthens the response. (Note: Negative reinforcement is not punishment.)

plain_en: bundled axons linking brain and body
definition: bundled axons that form neural cables connecting the central nervous system with muscles, glands, and sensory organs.

plain_en: body's electrochemical network of all nerve cells
definition: the body's speedy, electrochemical communication network, consisting of all the nerve cells of the peripheral and central nervous systems.

plain_en: childhood brain abnormalities affecting thinking and behavior
definition: central nervous system abnormalities (usually in the brain) that start in childhood and alter thinking and behavior (as in intellectual limitations or a psychological disorder).

plain_en: creation of new nerve cells
definition: the formation of new neurons.

plain_en: nerve cell, the basic unit of the nervous system
definition: a nerve cell; the basic building block of the nervous system.

plain_en: brain's ability to reorganize and form new pathways
definition: the brain's ability to change, especially during childhood, by reorganizing after damage or by building new pathways based on experience.

plain_en: chemicals carrying messages across synapses between neurons
definition: chemical messengers that cross the synaptic gaps between neurons. When released by the sending neuron, neurotransmitters travel across the synapse and bind to receptor sites on the receiving neuron, thereby influencing whether that neuron will generate a neural impulse.

plain_en: stimulus that triggers no response before conditioning
definition: in classical conditioning, a stimulus that elicits no response before conditioning.

plain_en: symmetrical bell-shaped distribution with most scores near mean
definition: a symmetrical, bell-shaped curve that describes the distribution of many types of data; most scores fall near the mean (about 68 percent fall within one standard deviation of it) and fewer and fewer scores lie near the extremes. (Also called a normal distribution.)

plain_en: conforming to gain approval or avoid disapproval
definition: influence resulting from a person's desire to gain approval or avoid disapproval.

plain_en: society's understood rules for expected behavior
definition: a society's understood rules for accepted and expected behavior. Norms prescribe "proper" behavior in individual and social situations.

plain_en: sleep stages other than rapid eye movement sleep
definition: non-rapid eye movement sleep; encompasses all sleep stages except for REM sleep.

plain_en: framing choices to encourage beneficial decisions
definition: framing choices in a way that encourages people to make beneficial decisions.

plain_en: following an order or command
definition: complying with an order or a command.

plain_en: body mass index of 30 or higher
definition: defined as a body mass index (BMI) measurement of 30 or higher, which is calculated from our weight-to-height ratio. (Individuals who are overweight have a BMI of 25 or higher.)

plain_en: knowing things exist even when unseen
definition: the awareness that things continue to exist even when not perceived.

plain_en: learning by watching others
definition: learning by observing others. (Also called social learning.)

plain_en: unwanted repetitive thoughts and/or actions
definition: a disorder characterized by unwanted repetitive thoughts (obsessions), actions (compulsions), or both.

plain_en: back-of-head cortex area handling visual information
definition: the portion of the cerebral cortex lying at the back of the head; it includes areas that receive information from the visual fields.

plain_en: the sense of smell
definition: our sense of smell.

plain_en: speech stage around ages 1-2 using single words
definition: the stage in speech development, from about age 1 to 2, during which a child speaks mostly in single words.

plain_en: behavior that produces an environmental consequence
definition: behavior that operates on the environment, producing a consequence.

plain_en: chamber where animals press levers for rewards
definition: in operant conditioning research, a chamber (also known as a Skinner box) containing a bar or key that an animal can manipulate to obtain a food or water reinforcer; attached devices record the animal's rate of bar pressing or key pecking.

plain_en: learning shaped by consequences like rewards and punishments
definition: a type of learning in which a behavior becomes more likely to recur if followed by a reinforcer or less likely to recur if followed by a punisher.

plain_en: precise statement of procedures used in research
definition: a carefully worded statement of the exact procedures (operations) used in a research study. For example, human intelligence may be operationally defined as what an intelligence test measures. (Also known as operationalization.)

plain_en: opium-derived drugs that reduce pain and anxiety
definition: opium and its derivatives; they depress neural activity, temporarily lessening pain and anxiety.

plain_en: opposing color pairs enable color vision
definition: the theory that opposing retinal processes (red-green, blue-yellow, white-black) enable color vision. For example, some cells are stimulated by green and inhibited by red; others are stimulated by red and inhibited by green.

plain_en: carries visual signals from eye to brain
definition: the nerve that carries neural impulses from the eye to the brain.

plain_en: studies how organizations affect workers and change
definition: an I/O psychology subfield that examines organizational influences on worker satisfaction and productivity and facilitates organizational change.

plain_en: deliberately excluding people from a group
definition: deliberate social exclusion of individuals or groups.

plain_en: better memory for faces of one's own race
definition: the tendency to recall faces of one's own race more accurately than faces of other races. Also called the cross-race effect and the own-race bias.

plain_en: people seen as different from our group
definition: "them" -those perceived as different or apart from our ingroup.

plain_en: overestimating how right our beliefs are
definition: the tendency to be more confident than correct -to overestimate the accuracy of our beliefs and judgments.

plain_en: sudden intense fear attacks with physical symptoms
