definition: an anxiety disorder marked by unpredictable, minutes-long episodes of intense dread in which a person may experience terror and accompanying chest pain, choking, or other frightening sensations; often followed by worry over a possible next attack.

plain_en: handling many parts of a stimulus at once
definition: processing multiple aspects of a stimulus or problem simultaneously.

plain_en: calms the body and saves energy
definition: the division of the autonomic nervous system that calms the body, conserving its energy.

plain_en: top-rear cortex area for touch and body position
definition: the portion of the cerebral cortex lying at the top of the head and toward the rear; it receives sensory input for touch and body position.

plain_en: rewarding only sometimes; slower learning, slower fading
definition: reinforcing a response only part of the time; results in slower acquisition of a response but much greater resistance to extinction than does continuous reinforcement.

plain_en: intense absorbed early romantic attraction
definition: an aroused state of intense positive absorption in another, usually present at the beginning of a romantic relationship.

plain_en: experts who judge a study's quality
definition: scientific experts who evaluate a research article's theory, originality, and accuracy.

plain_en: percent of scores below a given score
definition: the percentage of scores that are lower than a given score.

plain_en: brain organizing and interpreting sensory input
definition: the process by which our brain organizes and interprets sensory information, enabling us to recognize objects and events as meaningful.

plain_en: adjusting to altered sensory input
definition: the ability to adjust to changed sensory input, including an artificially displaced or even inverted visual field.

plain_en: seeing objects as stable despite changing images
definition: perceiving objects as unchanging (having consistent color, brightness, shape, and size) even as illumination and retinal images change.

plain_en: mental readiness to see one thing, not another
definition: a mental predisposition to perceive one thing and not another.

plain_en: nerves linking brain and spinal cord to body
definition: the sensory and motor neurons that connect the central nervous system (CNS) to the rest of the body.

plain_en: persuasion via incidental cues like attractiveness
definition: occurs when people are influenced by incidental cues, such as a speaker's attractiveness.

plain_en: long-lasting depressed mood for two or more years
definition: a disorder in which people experience a depressed mood on more days than not for at least 2 years (formerly called dysthymia.)

plain_en: forming impressions of ourselves and others
definition: how we form impressions of ourselves and others, including attributions of behavior.

plain_en: Rogers therapy using empathy and active listening
definition: a humanistic therapy, developed by Carl Rogers, in which the therapist uses techniques such as active listening within an accepting, genuine, empathic environment to facilitate clients' growth. (Also called client-centered therapy.)

plain_en: feeling able to control one's environment
definition: our sense of controlling our environment rather than feeling helpless.

plain_en: a person's typical pattern of thinking and acting
definition: an individual's characteristic pattern of thinking, feeling, and acting.

plain_en: rigid, enduring behavior patterns causing distress
definition: a group of disorders characterized by enduring inner experiences or behavior patterns that differ from someone's cultural norms and expectations, are pervasive and inflexible, begin in adolescence or early adulthood, are stable over time, and cause distress or impairment.

plain_en: questionnaire measuring personality traits
definition: a questionnaire (often with true-false or agree-disagree items) on which people respond to items designed to gauge a wide range of feelings and behaviors; used to assess selected personality traits.

plain_en: scientific study of personality
definition: the scientific study of personality and its development, structure, traits, processes, variations, and disordered forms (personality disorders).

plain_en: I/O subfield for hiring, training, and evaluating workers
definition: an I/O psychology subfield that helps with job seeking, and with employee recruitment, selection, placement, training, appraisal, and development.

plain_en: changing attitudes to influence actions
definition: changing people's attitudes, potentially influencing their actions.

plain_en: brain scan showing where glucose is used
definition: technique for detecting brain activity that displays where a radioactive form of glucose goes while the brain performs a given task.

plain_en: illusion of motion from blinking lights
definition: an illusion of movement created when two or more adjacent lights blink on and off in quick succession.

plain_en: smallest distinct sound unit in language
definition: in a language, the smallest distinctive sound unit.

plain_en: briefly holds sounds in memory
definition: a memory component that briefly holds auditory information.

plain_en: basic bodily requirement
definition: a basic bodily requirement.

plain_en: how high or low a tone sounds
definition: a tone's experienced highness or lowness; depends on frequency.

plain_en: pitch depends on where cochlea is stimulated
definition: in hearing, the theory that links the pitch we hear with the place where the cochlea's membrane is stimulated. (Also called place coding.)

plain_en: results caused by expectation alone
definition: experimental results caused by expectations alone; any effect on behavior caused by the administration of an inert substance or condition, which the recipient assumes is an active agent.

plain_en: machine measuring body changes to detect lies
definition: a machine used in attempts to detect lies; measures emotion-linked changes in perspiration, heart rate, and breathing.

plain_en: whole group from which samples are drawn
definition: all those in a group being studied, from which samples may be drawn. (Note: Except for national studies, this does not refer to a country's whole population.)

plain_en: study of strengths and well-being
definition: the scientific study of human flourishing, with the goals of promoting strengths and virtues that foster well-being, resilience, and positive emotions, and that help individuals and communities to thrive.

plain_en: rewarding a behavior increases it
definition: increasing behaviors by presenting a pleasurable stimulus. A positive reinforcer is any stimulus that, when presented after a response, strengthens the response.

plain_en: hypnotist's instruction to act later
definition: a suggestion, made during a hypnosis session, to be carried out after the subject is no longer hypnotized; used by some clinicians to help control undesired symptoms and behaviors.

plain_en: personal growth after severe hardship
definition: positive psychological changes following a struggle with extremely challenging circumstances and life crises.

plain_en: lasting trauma symptoms after a terrifying event
definition: a disorder characterized by haunting memories, nightmares, hypervigilance, avoidance of trauma-related stimuli, social withdrawal, jumpy anxiety, numbness of feeling, and/or insomnia that lingers for four weeks or more after a traumatic experience.

plain_en: test predicts what it should
definition: the success with which a test predicts the behavior it is designed to predict; it is assessed by computing the correlation between test scores and the criterion behavior. (Also called criterion-related validity.)

plain_en: unjustified negative attitude toward a group
definition: an unjustifiable and usually negative attitude toward a group and its members. Prejudice generally involves negative emotions, stereotyped beliefs, and a predisposition to discriminatory action.

plain_en: early childhood stage before logical thinking
definition: in Piaget's theory, the stage (from about 2 to 6 or 7 years of age) at which a child learns to use language but does not yet comprehend the mental operations of concrete logic.

plain_en: built-in readiness to learn survival associations
definition: a biological predisposition to learn associations, such as between taste and nausea, that have survival value.

plain_en: innate reward satisfying biological needs
definition: an innately reinforcing stimulus, such as one that satisfies a biological need.

plain_en: body parts enabling reproduction
definition: the body structures (ovaries, testes, and external genitalia) that make sexual reproduction possible.

plain_en: unconscious activation of associations
definition: the activation, often unconsciously, of certain associations, thus predisposing one's perception, memory, or response.

plain_en: old learning blocks new memories
definition: the forward-acting disruptive effect of older learning on the recall of new information.

plain_en: tackling the stressor directly
definition: attempting to alleviate stress directly -by changing the stressor or the way we interact with that stressor.

plain_en: ambiguous images reveal inner feelings
definition: a personality test, such as the TAT or Rorschach, that provides ambiguous images designed to trigger projection of one's inner dynamics and explore the preconscious and unconscious mind.

plain_en: helpful, constructive behavior
definition: positive, constructive, helpful behavior. The opposite of antisocial behavior.

plain_en: best mental example of a category
definition: a mental image or best example of a category. Matching new items to a prototype provides a quick and easy method for sorting items into categories (as when comparing feathered creatures to a prototypical bird, such as a crow).

plain_en: substance altering brain and mood
definition: a chemical substance that alters the brain, causing changes in perceptions and moods.

plain_en: Freud's theory of unconscious motives
definition: Freud's theory of personality that attributes thoughts and actions to unconscious motives and conflicts; the techniques used in treating psychological disorders by seeking to expose and interpret unconscious tensions.

plain_en: Freud's therapy releasing repressed feelings
definition: Sigmund Freud's therapeutic technique. Freud believed the patient's free associations, resistances, dreams, and transferences -and the analyst's interpretations of them -released previously repressed feelings, allowing the patient to gain self-insight.

plain_en: personality theories stressing unconscious and childhood
definition: theories that view personality with a focus on the unconscious mind and the importance of childhood experiences.

plain_en: insight therapy from psychoanalytic tradition
definition: therapy deriving from the psychoanalytic tradition; views individuals as responding to unconscious forces and childhood experiences, and seeks to enhance self-insight.

plain_en: distressing disturbance impairing daily life
definition: a disturbance in people's thoughts, emotions, or behaviors that causes distress or suffering and impairs their daily lives.

plain_en: science of behavior and mental processes
definition: the science of behavior and mental processes.

plain_en: science of measuring abilities and traits
definition: the scientific study of the measurement of human abilities, attitudes, and traits.

plain_en: mind, nerves, hormones affect immunity
definition: the study of how psychological, neural, and endocrine processes together affect our immune system and resulting health.

plain_en: study of drugs' effects on mind
definition: the study of the effects of drugs on mind and behavior.

plain_en: linking stimulus intensity to experience
definition: the study of relationships between the physical characteristics of stimuli, such as their intensity, and our psychological experience of them.

plain_en: brain surgery to change behavior
definition: surgery that removes or destroys brain tissue in an effort to change behavior.

plain_en: psychological treatment through therapist interaction
definition: treatment involving psychological techniques; consists of interactions between a trained therapist and someone seeking to overcome psychological difficulties or achieve personal growth.

plain_en: disorders with lost contact with reality
definition: a group of disorders marked by irrational ideas, distorted perceptions, and a loss of contact with reality.

plain_en: period of sexual maturation
definition: the period of sexual maturation, during which a person usually becomes capable of reproducing.

plain_en: event that decreases a behavior
definition: an event that tends to decrease the behavior that it follows.

plain_en: eye opening letting light in
definition: the adjustable opening in the center of the eye through which light enters.

plain_en: non-numerical, narrative research data
definition: a research method that relies on in-depth, narrative data that are not translated into numbers.

plain_en: numerical data research
definition: a research method that relies on quantifiable, numerical data.

plain_en: chance placement into experimental groups
definition: assigning participants to experimental and control groups by chance, thus minimizing preexisting differences between the different groups.

plain_en: everyone has equal chance of selection
definition: a sample that fairly represents a population because each member has an equal chance of inclusion.

plain_en: highest minus lowest score
definition: the difference between the highest and lowest scores in a distribution.

plain_en: confrontational therapy challenging illogical beliefs
definition: a confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Albert Ellis, that vigorously challenges people's illogical, self-defeating attitudes and assumptions.

plain_en: retrieving stored information without cues
definition: a measure of memory in which the person must retrieve information learned earlier, as on a fill-in-the-blank test.

plain_en: behavior, thoughts, and environment all affect each other
definition: the interacting influences of behavior, internal cognition, and environment.

plain_en: help those who helped you
definition: an expectation that people will help, not hurt, those who have helped them.

plain_en: identifying previously learned items from options
definition: a measure of memory in which the person identifies items previously learned, as on a multiple-choice test.

plain_en: retrieved memories may change before restorage
definition: a process in which previously stored memories, when retrieved, are potentially altered before being stored again.

plain_en: automatic reaction to a sensory stimulus
definition: a simple, automatic response to a sensory stimulus, such as the knee-jerk response.

plain_en: brief resting pause after a neuron fires
definition: in neural processing, a brief resting pause that occurs after a neuron has fired; subsequent action potentials cannot occur until the axon returns to its resting state.

plain_en: extreme scores tend to drift toward average
definition: the tendency for extreme or unusual scores or events to fall back (regress) toward the average.

plain_en: event that strengthens the behavior it follows
definition: in operant conditioning, any event that strengthens the behavior it follows.

plain_en: pattern defining how often responses are reinforced
definition: a pattern that defines how often a desired response will be reinforced.

plain_en: harming someone's relationships or social standing
definition: an act of aggression (physical or verbal) intended to harm a person's relationship or social standing.

plain_en: feeling worse off than those we compare with
definition: the perception that we are worse off relative to those with whom we compare ourselves.

plain_en: time saved when learning material again
definition: a measure of memory that assesses the amount of time saved when learning material again.

plain_en: test yields consistent results
definition: the extent to which a test yields consistent results, as assessed by the consistency of scores on two halves of the test, on alternative forms of the test, or on retesting.

plain_en: more REM sleep after REM deprivation
definition: the tendency for REM sleep to increase following REM sleep deprivation.

plain_en: sleep stage with vivid dreams and relaxed muscles
definition: rapid eye movement sleep; a recurring sleep stage during which vivid dreams commonly occur. Also known as paradoxical sleep, because the muscles are relaxed (except for minor twitches) but other body systems are active. (Sometimes called R sleep.)

plain_en: acting out dreams because REM paralysis fails
definition: a sleep disorder in which normal REM paralysis does not occur; instead, twitching, talking, or even kicking or punching may occur, often acting out one's dream.

plain_en: repeating a study to check findings
definition: repeating the essence of a research study, usually with different participants in different situations, to see whether the basic finding can be reproduced.

plain_en: judging likelihood by how well something matches a prototype
definition: judging the likelihood of events in terms of how well they seem to represent, or match, particular prototypes; may lead us to ignore other relevant information.

plain_en: banishing anxiety-arousing thoughts from consciousness
definition: in psychoanalytic theory, the basic defense mechanism that banishes from consciousness anxiety-arousing thoughts, feelings, and memories.

plain_en: personal strength to cope and recover from adversity
definition: the personal strength that helps people cope with stress and recover from adversity and even trauma.

plain_en: blocking anxiety-laden material from consciousness
definition: in psychoanalysis, the blocking from consciousness of anxiety-laden material.

plain_en: automatic response to a stimulus
definition: behavior that occurs as an automatic response to some stimulus.

plain_en: nerve network filtering information and controlling arousal
definition: a nerve network that travels through the brainstem into the thalamus; it filters information and plays an important role in controlling arousal.

plain_en: light-sensitive back surface of the eye
definition: the light-sensitive back inner surface of the eye, containing the receptor rods and cones plus layers of neurons that begin the processing of visual information.

plain_en: depth cue from differing images in two eyes
definition: a binocular cue for perceiving depth. By comparing retinal images from the two eyes, the brain computes distance -the greater the disparity (difference) between the two images, the closer the object.

plain_en: getting information out of memory storage
definition: the process of getting information out of memory storage.

plain_en: new learning disrupts recall of old information
definition: the backward-acting disruptive effect of newer learning on the recall of old information.

plain_en: inability to remember one's past
definition: an inability to remember information from one's past.

plain_en: neurotransmitter reabsorbed by sending neuron
definition: a neurotransmitter's reabsorption by the sending neuron.

plain_en: retinal receptors for dim light and peripheral vision
definition: retinal receptors that detect black, white, and gray, and are sensitive to movement; necessary for peripheral and twilight vision, when cones don't respond.

plain_en: expected behaviors for a social position
definition: a set of expectations (norms) about a social position, defining how those in the position ought to behave.

plain_en: projective test using interpretations of inkblots
definition: a projective test designed by Hermann Rorschach; seeks to identify people's inner feelings by analyzing how they interpret 10 inkblots.

plain_en: compulsive overthinking about problems
definition: compulsive fretting; overthinking our problems and their causes.

plain_en: flawed sampling producing unrepresentative sample
definition: a flawed sampling process that produces an unrepresentative sample.

plain_en: limited mental ability but exceptional specific skill
definition: a condition in which a person otherwise limited in mental ability has an exceptional specific skill, such as in computation or drawing.

plain_en: temporary support for children's developing thinking
definition: in Vygotsky's theory, a framework that offers children temporary support as they develop higher levels of thinking.

plain_en: prejudice provides someone to blame
definition: the theory that prejudice offers an outlet for anger by providing someone to blame.

plain_en: graph of dots showing two variables' relationship
definition: a graphed cluster of dots, each of which represents the values of two variables. The slope of the points suggests the direction of the relationship between the two variables. The amount of scatter suggests the strength of the correlation (little scatter indicates high correlation).

plain_en: framework that organizes and interprets information
definition: a concept or framework that organizes and interprets information.

plain_en: mental disorders with delusions, hallucinations, and disorganized thinking
definition: a group of disorders characterized by delusions, hallucinations, disorganized thinking or speech, disorganized or unusual motor behavior, and negative symptoms (such as diminished emotional expression); includes schizophrenia and schizotypal personality disorder.

plain_en: physical traits of sexual maturity that don't involve reproduction
definition: nonreproductive sexual traits, such as female breasts and hips, male voice quality, and body hair.

plain_en: infants explore freely and are comforted by caregiver's return
definition: demonstrated by infants who comfortably explore environments in the presence of their caregiver, show only temporary distress when the caregiver leaves, and find comfort in the caregiver's return.

plain_en: focusing awareness on one particular stimulus
definition: focusing conscious awareness on a particular stimulus.

plain_en: the organizing center of personality, thoughts, feelings, and actions
definition: in modern psychology, assumed to be the center of personality, the organizer of our thoughts, feelings, and actions.

plain_en: motivation to fulfill one's potential after basic needs are met
definition: according to Maslow, one of the ultimate psychological needs that arises after basic physical and psychological needs are met and self-esteem is achieved; the motivation to fulfill one's potential.

plain_en: all thoughts and feelings about who we are
definition: all our thoughts and feelings about ourselves in answer to the question, "Who am I?"

plain_en: controlling impulses and delaying gratification for later rewards
definition: the ability to control impulses and delay short-term gratification for greater long-term rewards.

plain_en: we are motivated by needs for competence, autonomy, and relatedness
definition: the theory that we feel motivated to satisfy our needs for competence, autonomy, and relatedness.

plain_en: revealing intimate things about ourselves to others
definition: the act of revealing intimate aspects of ourselves to others.

plain_en: our sense of competence and effectiveness
definition: our sense of competence and effectiveness.

plain_en: our feelings of high or low self-worth
definition: our feelings of high or low self-worth.

plain_en: a belief that causes itself to come true
definition: a belief that leads to its own fulfillment.

plain_en: inaccurate reporting of one's own behavior
definition: bias when people report their behavior inaccurately.

plain_en: readiness to see ourselves favorably
definition: a readiness to perceive ourselves favorably.

plain_en: striving for meaning and purpose beyond the self
definition: according to Maslow, the striving for identity, meaning, and purpose beyond the self.

plain_en: explicit memory of facts and general knowledge
definition: explicit memory of facts and general knowledge; one of our two conscious memory systems (the other is episodic memory).

plain_en: sensory receptors and nervous system receive and represent stimuli
definition: the process by which our sensory receptors and nervous system receive and represent stimulus energies from our environment.

plain_en: infants know the world through senses and motor actions
definition: in Piaget's theory, the stage (from birth to nearly 2 years of age) at which infants know the world mostly in terms of their sensory impressions and motor activities.

plain_en: hearing loss from damage to cochlea or auditory nerve
definition: the most common form of hearing loss, caused by damage to the cochlea's receptor cells or to the auditory nerve; also called nerve deafness.

plain_en: neurons carrying incoming sensory information to brain and spinal cord
definition: neurons that carry incoming information from the body's tissues and sensory receptors to the brain and spinal cord.

plain_en: diminished sensitivity from constant stimulation
definition: diminished sensitivity as a consequence of constant stimulation.

plain_en: one sense influences another
definition: the principle that one sense may influence another, as when the smell of food influences its taste.

plain_en: immediate, very brief recording of sensory information
definition: the immediate, very brief recording of sensory information in the memory system.

plain_en: sensory nerve endings that respond to stimuli
definition: sensory nerve endings that respond to stimuli.

plain_en: processing one aspect at a time
definition: processing one aspect of a stimulus or problem at a time; generally used to process new information or to solve difficult problems.

plain_en: recalling first and last list items best
definition: our tendency to recall best the last items in a list initially (a recency effect) and the first items in a list after a delay (a primacy effect).

plain_en: weight thermostat point the body defends
definition: the point at which the "weight thermostat" may be set. When the body falls below this weight, increased hunger and a lowered metabolic rate may combine to restore lost weight.

plain_en: biologically influenced characteristics defining male, female, intersex
definition: in psychology, the biologically influenced characteristics by which people define male, female, and intersex.

plain_en: unwanted sexual behavior intended to harm
definition: any physical or verbal behavior of a sexual nature that is unwanted or intended to harm someone physically or emotionally. Can be expressed as either sexual harassment or sexual assault.

plain_en: sexual and emotional attraction to another person
definition: according to the APA (2015), "a person's sexual and emotional attraction to another person and the behavior and/or social affiliation that may result from this attraction."

plain_en: thoughts, feelings, and actions about physical attraction
definition: our thoughts, feelings, and actions related to our physical attraction to another.

plain_en: encoding based on structure or appearance of words
definition: encoding on a basic level, based on the structure or appearance of words.

plain_en: reinforcers guide behavior toward closer approximations of a target
definition: an operant conditioning procedure in which reinforcers guide behavior toward closer and closer approximations of the desired behavior.

plain_en: briefly activated memory of a few items
definition: briefly activated memory of a few items (such as digits of a phone number while calling) that is later stored or forgotten.

plain_en: detecting faint stimuli depends on experience, expectations, motivation, alertness
definition: a theory predicting how and when we detect the presence of a faint stimulus (signal) amid background stimulation (noise). Assumes there is no single absolute threshold and that detection depends partly on a person's experience, expectations, motivation, and alertness.

plain_en: participants don't know if they got treatment or placebo
definition: an experimental procedure in which the research participants are ignorant (blind) about whether they have received the treatment or a placebo.

plain_en: scores lacking symmetry around the average
definition: a representation of scores that lack symmetry around their average value.

plain_en: periodic, natural loss of consciousness
definition: a periodic, natural loss of consciousness -as distinct from unconsciousness resulting from a coma, general anesthesia, or hibernation. (Adapted from Dement, 1999.)

plain_en: breathing stops temporarily during sleep, causing awakenings
definition: a sleep disorder characterized by temporary cessations of breathing during sleep and repeated momentary awakenings.

plain_en: strong fear and avoidance of social settings
definition: intense fear and avoidance of social situations.

plain_en: culture's expected ages for major life events
definition: the culturally preferred timing of social events such as marriage, parenthood, and retirement.

plain_en: answering to match what researchers seem to want
definition: bias from people's responding in ways they presume a researcher expects or wishes.

plain_en: social behavior aims to maximize benefits and minimize costs
definition: the theory that our social behavior is an exchange process, the aim of which is to maximize benefits and minimize costs.

plain_en: others' presence helps easy tasks, hurts hard ones
definition: in the presence of others, improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks, and worsened performance on difficult tasks.

plain_en: self-concept part from group memberships
definition: the "we" aspect of our self-concept; the part of our answer to "Who am I?" that comes from our group memberships.

plain_en: group-focused leadership building teamwork and support
definition: group-oriented leadership that builds teamwork, mediates conflict, and offers support.

plain_en: we learn social behavior by observing and imitating others
definition: the theory that we learn social behavior by observing and imitating and by being rewarded or punished.

plain_en: group members put in less effort when pooled
definition: the tendency for people in a group to exert less effort when pooling their efforts toward attaining a common goal than when individually accountable.

plain_en: science of how people think about and influence each other
definition: the scientific study of how we think about, influence, and relate to one another.

plain_en: culturally learned guide for acting in situations
definition: a culturally modeled guide for how to act in various situations.

plain_en: both sides pursuing self-interest end up mutually harmed
definition: a situation in which two parties, by each pursuing their self-interest rather than the good of the group, become caught in mutually destructive behavior.

plain_en: behavior shaped by traits interacting with social context
definition: a view of behavior as influenced by the interaction between people's traits (including their thinking) and their social context.

plain_en: expectation to help those who need help
definition: an expectation that people will help those needing their help.

plain_en: peripheral division controlling skeletal muscles
definition: the division of the peripheral nervous system that controls the body's skeletal muscles. Also called the skeletal nervous system.

plain_en: cortex area registering body touch and movement
definition: a cerebral cortex area at the front of the parietal lobes that registers and processes body touch and movement sensations.

plain_en: forgetting where or how information was learned
definition: faulty memory for how, when, or where information was learned or imagined (as when misattributing information to a wrong source). Source amnesia, along with the misinformation effect, is at the heart of many false memories.

plain_en: spread-out study beats cramming for long-term memory
definition: the tendency for distributed study or practice to yield better long-term retention than is achieved through massed study or practice.

plain_en: persistent irrational fear of a specific thing
definition: an anxiety disorder marked by a persistent, irrational fear and avoidance of a specific object, activity, or situation.

plain_en: a male's first ejaculation
definition: [sperMAR-key] the first ejaculation.

plain_en: brain hemispheres isolated by cutting connecting fibers
definition: a condition resulting from surgery that isolates the brain's two hemispheres by cutting the fibers (mainly those of the corpus callosum) connecting them.

plain_en: weakened conditioned response returns after a pause
definition: the reappearance, after a pause, of a weakened conditioned response.

plain_en: overestimating how much others notice and judge us
definition: overestimating others' noticing and evaluating our appearance, performance, and blunders (as if we presume a spotlight shines on us).

plain_en: measure of how much scores vary around the mean
definition: a computed measure of how much scores vary around the mean score.

plain_en: uniform testing procedures with comparison scores from a pretested group
definition: defining uniform testing procedures and meaningful scores by comparison with the performance of a pretested group.

plain_en: Terman's American revision of Binet's intelligence test
definition: the widely used American revision (by Terman at Stanford University) of Binet's original intelligence test.

plain_en: likelihood a result occurred by chance
definition: a statistical statement of how likely it is that a result (such as a difference between samples) occurred by chance, assuming there is no difference between the populations being studied.

plain_en: generalized belief about a group of people
definition: a generalized (sometimes accurate but often overgeneralized) belief about a group of people.

plain_en: worry of confirming a negative stereotype about one's group
definition: a self-confirming concern that one will be evaluated based on a negative stereotype.

plain_en: drugs that excite neural activity and speed body functions
definition: drugs that excite neural activity and speed up body functions.

plain_en: any event or situation that evokes a response
definition: any event or situation that evokes a response.

plain_en: retaining encoded information over time
definition: the process of retaining encoded information over time.

plain_en: procedure observing infant reactions to caregiver leaving and returning
definition: a procedure for studying child-caregiver attachment; a child is placed in an unfamiliar environment while their caregiver leaves and then returns, and the child's reactions are observed.

plain_en: infants' fear of unfamiliar people, starting around 8 months
definition: the fear of strangers that infants commonly display, beginning by about 8 months of age.

plain_en: perceiving and responding to threatening or challenging events
definition: the process by which we perceive and respond to certain events, called stressors, that we appraise as threatening or challenging.

plain_en: illusion of movement from rapid still images
definition: an illusion of continuous movement (as in a motion picture) experienced when viewing a rapid series of slightly varying still images.

plain_en: same job-relevant questions asked of all applicants
definition: an interview process that asks the same job-relevant questions of all applicants, each of whom is rated on established scales.

plain_en: self-perceived happiness or life satisfaction
definition: self-perceived happiness or satisfaction with life. Used along with measures of objective well-being (for example, physical and economic indicators) to evaluate people's quality of life.

plain_en: below the threshold for conscious awareness
definition: below one's absolute threshold for conscious awareness.

plain_en: continued substance use despite major life disruption
definition: a disorder characterized by continued substance use despite significant life disruption.

plain_en: internalized ideals and conscience guiding judgment
definition: the partly conscious part of personality that, according to Freud, represents internalized ideals and provides standards for judgment (the conscience) and for future aspirations.

plain_en: shared goals requiring people to cooperate
definition: shared goals that override differences among people and require their cooperation.

plain_en: brain cluster controlling sleep-wake rhythm via light
definition: a pair of cell clusters in the hypothalamus that controls circadian rhythm. In response to light, the SCN adjusts melatonin production, thus modifying our feelings of sleepiness.

plain_en: questioning a sample about attitudes or behaviors
definition: a non-experimental technique for obtaining the self-reported attitudes or behaviors of a particular group, usually by questioning a representative, random sample of the group.

plain_en: autonomic division that arouses and energizes the body
definition: the division of the autonomic nervous system that arouses the body, mobilizing its energy.

plain_en: junction where neurons communicate across a tiny gap
definition: [SIN-aps] the junction between the axon tip of the sending neuron and the dendrite or cell body of the receiving neuron. The tiny gap at this junction is called the synaptic gap or synaptic cleft.

plain_en: pairing relaxation with gradually increasing anxiety triggers
definition: a type of exposure therapy that associates a pleasant relaxed state with gradually increasing anxiety-triggering stimuli. Commonly used to treat specific phobias.

plain_en: goal-focused leadership that organizes work and sets standards
definition: goal-oriented leadership that sets standards, organizes work, and focuses attention on goals.

plain_en: early speech using mostly nouns and verbs
definition: the early speech stage in which a child speaks like a telegram - "go car" -using mostly nouns and verbs.

plain_en: characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity
definition: a person's characteristic emotional reactivity and intensity.

plain_en: cortex above the ears for hearing and language
definition: the portion of the cerebral cortex lying roughly above the ears; it includes the auditory areas, each of which receives information primarily from the opposite ear. They also enable language processing.

plain_en: stress response of nurturing and seeking social support
definition: under stress, people (especially women) may nurture themselves and others (tend) and bond with and seek support from others (befriend).

plain_en: harmful agents reaching embryo or fetus prenatally
definition: agents, such as chemicals and viruses, that can reach the embryo or fetus during prenatal development and cause harm.

plain_en: theory of anxiety about death reminders
definition: a theory of death-related anxiety; explores people's emotional and behavioral responses to reminders of their impending death.

plain_en: better memory after retrieving than rereading
definition: enhanced memory after retrieving, rather than simply rereading, information. Also referred to as a retrieval practice effect or test-enhanced learning.

plain_en: key male sex hormone present in both sexes
definition: the most important male sex hormone. Males and females have it, but the additional testosterone in males stimulates the growth of the male sex organs during the fetal period and the development of male sex characteristics during puberty.

plain_en: forebrain sensory relay center atop the brainstem
definition: [THAL-uh-muss] the forebrain's sensory control center, located on top of the brainstem; it directs messages to the sensory receiving areas in the cortex and transmits replies to the cerebellum and medulla.

plain_en: projective test using stories about ambiguous scenes
definition: a projective test in which people express their inner feelings and interests through the stories they make up about ambiguous scenes.

plain_en: integrated explanation organizing observations and predicting events
definition: an explanation using an integrated set of principles that organizes observations and predicts behaviors or events.

plain_en: ideas about one's own and others' mental states
definition: people's ideas about their own and others' mental states -about their feelings, perceptions, and thoughts, and the behaviors these might predict.

plain_en: trusting bond between therapist and client
definition: a bond of trust and mutual understanding between a therapist and client, who work together constructively to overcome the client's problem.

plain_en: stimulation level needed to trigger a neural impulse
definition: the level of stimulation required to trigger a neural impulse.

plain_en: place with clearly defined, reliably enforced norms
definition: a place with clearly defined and reliably imposed norms.

plain_en: earning tokens for desired behavior, exchanged for rewards
definition: an operant conditioning procedure in which people earn a token for exhibiting a desired behavior and can later exchange tokens for privileges or treats.

plain_en: diminished drug effect requiring larger doses
definition: the diminishing effect with regular use of the same dose of a drug, requiring the user to take larger and larger doses before experiencing the drug's effect.

plain_en: perception guided by experience and expectations
definition: information processing guided by higher-level mental processes, as when we construct perceptions drawing on our experience and expectations.

plain_en: characteristic pattern of behavior or disposition
definition: a characteristic pattern of behavior or a disposition to feel and act in certain ways, as assessed by self-report inventories and peer reports.

plain_en: magnetic pulses used to stimulate or suppress brain activity
definition: the application of repeated pulses of magnetic energy to the brain; used to stimulate or suppress brain activity.

plain_en: converting physical energy into neural impulses
definition: conversion of one form of energy into another. In sensation, the transforming of physical energy, such as sights, sounds, and smells, into neural impulses the brain can interpret.

plain_en: patient transfers feelings about others onto analyst
definition: in psychoanalysis, the patient's transfer to the analyst of emotions linked with other relationships (such as love or hatred for a parent).

plain_en: distress following exposure to traumatic or stressful events
definition: a group of disorders in which exposure to a traumatic or stressful event is followed by psychological distress.

plain_en: speech stage using mostly two-word statements
definition: beginning about age 2, the stage in speech development during which a child speaks mostly in two-word statements.

plain_en: competitive, impatient, anger-prone personality style
definition: Friedman and Rosenman's term for competitive, hard-driving, impatient, verbally aggressive, and anger-prone people.

plain_en: easygoing, relaxed personality style
definition: Friedman and Rosenman's term for easygoing, relaxed people.

plain_en: caring, accepting, nonjudgmental attitude aiding self-acceptance
definition: a caring, accepting, nonjudgmental attitude, which Carl Rogers believed would help clients develop self-awareness and self-acceptance. (Also known as unconditional regard.)

plain_en: natural unlearned response to a stimulus
definition: in classical conditioning, an unlearned, naturally occurring response (such as salivation) to an unconditioned stimulus (UCS) (such as food in the mouth).

plain_en: stimulus that naturally and automatically triggers a response
definition: in classical conditioning, a stimulus that unconditionally -naturally and automatically -triggers an unconditioned response UCR).

plain_en: hidden thoughts and memories outside awareness
definition: according to Freud, a reservoir of mostly unacceptable thoughts, wishes, feelings, and memories. According to contemporary psychologists, information processing of which we are unaware.

plain_en: innate grasp of grammar rules across languages
definition: humans' innate predisposition to understand the principles and rules that govern grammar in all languages.

plain_en: extent a test measures what it should
definition: the extent to which a test or experiment measures or predicts what it is supposed to. (See also predictive validity.)

plain_en: anything measurable that can change
definition: anything that can vary and is feasible and ethical to measure.

plain_en: reward after unpredictable time periods
definition: in operant conditioning, a reinforcement schedule that reinforces a response at unpredictable time intervals.

plain_en: reward after unpredictable number of responses
definition: in operant conditioning, a reinforcement schedule that reinforces a response after an unpredictable number of responses.

plain_en: sense of balance and body position
definition: our balance sense; our sense of body movement and position that enables our sense of balance.

plain_en: treating fears with simulated electronic environments
definition: a counterconditioning technique that treats anxiety through creative electronic simulations in which people can safely face specific fears, such as flying, spiders, or public speaking.

plain_en: device testing depth perception in infants
definition: a laboratory device for testing depth perception in infants and young animals.

plain_en: briefly holds visual and spatial information
definition: a memory component that briefly holds information about objects' appearance and location in space.

plain_en: distance between wave peaks
definition: the distance from the peak of one light or sound wave to the peak of the next. Electromagnetic wavelengths vary from the short gamma waves to the long pulses of radio transmission.

plain_en: difference must be a constant percentage
definition: the principle that, to be perceived as different, two stimuli must differ by a constant minimum percentage (rather than a constant amount).

plain_en: widely used intelligence test with verbal and nonverbal parts
definition: the WAIS and its companion versions for children are the most widely used intelligence tests; they contain verbal and performance (nonverbal) subtests.

plain_en: brain area for language comprehension
definition: a brain area, usually in the left temporal lobe, involved in language comprehension and expression.

plain_en: distress after stopping an addictive substance
definition: the discomfort and distress that follow discontinuing an addictive drug or behavior.

plain_en: active processing of sensory and retrieved information
definition: a newer understanding of short-term memory; conscious, active processing of both (1) incoming sensory information, and (2) information retrieved from long-term memory.

plain_en: sex chromosome present in both sexes
definition: the sex chromosome found in females and males. Females typically have two X chromosomes; males typically have one. An X chromosome from each parent produces a female child.

plain_en: sex chromosome typically found only in males
definition: the sex chromosome typically found only in males. When paired with an X chromosome from the mother, it produces a male child.

plain_en: performance rises with arousal, then drops
definition: the principle that performance increases with arousal only up to a point, beyond which performance decreases.

plain_en: retina has red, green, and blue receptors
definition: the theory that the retina contains three different types of color receptors -one most sensitive to red, one to green, one to blue -which, when stimulated in combination, can produce the perception of any color.
